title: What does ConfidentialMPTClawback do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of ConfidentialMPTClawback and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, ConfidentialMPTClawback removes a holder's confidential MPT balance under the issuance's clawback authority. [1]

The documented operation acts on the confidential balance and removes it from circulation. Its confidentiality proofs and issuance permissions differ from a public trust-line clawback. Review the holder and issuance identifiers together with the feature's prerequisites. This is a specific issuer capability, not a generic method of reversing anonymous XRP payments. [1]

The ConfidentialMPTClawback reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using ConfidentialMPTClawback, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
